title: Explicit quotient-Jacobian minor formula for linear combinations
statement:
Let $F$ be a field, $n,s,l\geq0$, $T=F[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], and $I\subseteq T$ an ideal. Let $f_1,\ldots,f_s\in I$, let $C=(c_{ab})$ be an $l\times s$ matrix over $T$ [def-weil-matrix], and put $g_a=\sum_{b=1}^s c_{ab}f_b$. Write $\partial_i$ for termwise differentiation [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative], $\pi:T\to R=T/I$ for the quotient map, and $J_x(h)=(\pi(\partial_i h_a))_{a,i}$ for the quotient Jacobian of any finite list $h$ (rows are list entries). Then for every $a,i$,
$$\partial_i g_a=\sum_b c_{ab}\partial_i f_b+\sum_b(\partial_i c_{ab})f_b,\qquad J_x(g)=\overline C J_x(f),$$
where $\overline C=(\pi(c_{ab}))$. For every $r\geq0$ and subsets $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,l\}$, $B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ of cardinality $r$, with all index sets in increasing order, one has
$$\det(J_x(g)_{A,B})=\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,s\}\\|S|=r}}\det(\overline C_{A,S})\det(J_x(f)_{S,B})\quad\text{in }R.$$
Here subscripts denote submatrices [def-weil-submatrix] and $\det$ is [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]. The formula includes $r=0$ (empty determinants are $1$) and $s<r$ (the sum is empty and the left side is $0$). Neither list is required to generate $I$.

proof.text: By [def-trf-formal-power-series-partial-derivative], each $\partial_i$ is an $F$-derivation. The definition of derivation in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] gives additivity and $\partial_i(uv)=u\partial_i v+v\partial_i u$. Apply additivity repeatedly to the finite sum defining $g_a$ and the product rule to each $c_{ab}f_b$. Commutativity of $T$ and distribution of the finite sum give $\partial_i g_a=\sum_b c_{ab}\partial_i f_b+\sum_b(\partial_i c_{ab})f_b$. The empty sum is zero, so this calculation includes $s=0$.

source.place: Tag 0C4B (lemma-fitting-ideal-well-defined), generator-change paragraph and displayed derivative-error matrix.

proof.text: Apply the quotient ring homomorphism $\pi$ to the identity in step 1. Since each $f_b\in I$, its residue is zero, hence $\pi((\partial_i c_{ab})f_b)=\pi(\partial_i c_{ab})\pi(f_b)=0$. Preservation of sums and products gives $\pi(\partial_i g_a)=\sum_b\pi(c_{ab})\pi(\partial_i f_b)$. With matrix entries as in [def-weil-matrix], this is precisely $J_x(g)=\overline C J_x(f)$, where the entry of the product in row $a$, column $i$ is the displayed sum. No condition that either list generates $I$ was used.

source.place: Tag 0C4B (lemma-fitting-ideal-well-defined), generator-change paragraph and displayed derivative-error matrix.

proof.text: Fix $A,B$ of cardinality $r$, with increasing enumerations $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ and $b_1,\ldots,b_r$. Define the $r\times s$ matrix $U_{t,j}=\pi(c_{a_tj})$ and the $s\times r$ matrix $V_{j,u}=\pi(\partial_{b_u}f_j)$. Step 2 gives $(UV)_{t,u}=J_x(g)_{a_t,b_u}$, so $UV=J_x(g)_{A,B}$ by [def-weil-submatrix]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cauchy-binet] over the commutative ring $R=T/I$, with its $m=r$ and $n=s$. For each increasing $r$-element subset $S$ of $\{1,\ldots,s\}$, its column submatrix $U^S$ has entries $\overline C_{a_t,j}$ for $j\in S$, hence is $\overline C_{A,S}$; its row submatrix $V_S$ is $J_x(f)_{S,B}$. Substituting these entrywise equalities into that node's determinant formula proves the required selected-minor identity.

source.place: Tag 0F0K (item-cauchy-binet), applied to the selected rows and columns of the product in Curves Tag 0C4B.

proof.text: If $r=0$, [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] makes every empty determinant $1$, and there is exactly one subset $S$ of size zero, so the sum is $1$. If $s<r$, there is no $r$-element subset of the $s$-element index set; the sum in step 3 is zero, giving a zero left determinant. If $r>l$ or $r>n$, there are no choices of $A,B$ as required and the assertion about such choices is vacuous.

lean.statement: theorem formalJacobian_generator_minor_expansion (F : Type u) [Field F] (n s l : ℕ) (I : Ideal (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F)) (f : Fin s → MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F) (hf : ∀ b : Fin s, f b ∈ I) (C : Matrix (Fin l) (Fin s) (MvPowerSeries (Fin n) F)) : (∀ (a : Fin l) (i : Fin n), pderiv F i (∑ b : Fin s, C a b * f b) = (∑ b : Fin s, C a b * pderiv F i (f b)) + ∑ b : Fin s, pderiv F i (C a b) * f b) ∧ (Matrix.of (fun a i ↦ Ideal.Quotient.mk I (pderiv F i (∑ b : Fin s, C a b * f b))) = C.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) * Matrix.of (fun b i ↦ Ideal.Quotient.mk I (pderiv F i (f b)))) ∧ (∀ (r : ℕ) (A : Finset (Fin l)) (B : Finset (Fin n)) (hA : A.card = r) (hB : B.card = r), (Matrix.submatrix (Matrix.of (fun a i ↦ Ideal.Quotient.mk I (pderiv F i (∑ b : Fin s, C a b * f b)))) (A.orderEmbOfFin hA) (B.orderEmbOfFin hB)).det = ∑ S : {S : Finset (Fin s) // S.card = r}, ((C.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).submatrix (A.orderEmbOfFin hA) (S.val.orderEmbOfFin S.property)).det * (Matrix.submatrix (Matrix.of (fun b i ↦ Ideal.Quotient.mk I (pderiv F i (f b)))) (S.val.orderEmbOfFin S.property) (B.orderEmbOfFin hB)).det)
